From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Production: sudden 429 spikes and timeouts (North America)

Triage findings (short):
- Root cause: routing label regression from 2027-08-20 config push. The org->project mapping for HealthBridge still had the legacy label 'hb_v1' flagged as both a project-level and org-level counter, causing requests to be counted twice against quota windows.
- Effect: token bucket refill calculation saw higher withdrawal rate and flipped the tenant into hard throttle for their mid-day traffic pattern. Client retries then created a feedback loop.

Completed actions:
- Flipped fallback to canonical mapping for HealthBridge at 09:00 PDT (safe rollback) — immediate 60% drop in 429 rate in canary region. See attached rate_snapshot_08-27.csv for delta.
- Implemented a temporary tolerance rule to ignore duplicate counters for 24 hours while we push a proper fix.
- Added a server-side soft-retry header (Retry-After: 2s) for their tenant to encourage client backoff.

Next steps:
- Engineering will deploy a patch this afternoon to remove counting duplication at the metric aggregation layer (JIRA INF-4321).
- Ops: recommend a one-time emergency throughput increase if customer still sees residual errors after patch; Marissa to coordinate approvals.

Attachments referenced: rate_snapshot_08-27.csv

—Rishi
Lead SRE, Inference Runtime

[attachment: rate_snapshot_08-27.csv (text/csv, 45KB)]

Vivek — quick summary and recommended asks for exec sign-off: 

What happened: a routing-label regression caused duplicate request counting at both project and org counters for HealthBridge, triggering tenant-level hard throttling during peak traffic which was amplified by client retries. Customers saw elevated 429s and upstream timeouts for ~40 minutes before canary rollback.

Impact: short-term user-visible degradation across two ops-critical services. We prevented a widespread outage; however this is a material commercial risk given their pending Dedicated commitment.

Engineering mitigations already executed:
- Canary rollback to canonical mapping (reduced 429s by ~60% in canary).
- Temporary ignore-duplicates rule for 24h.
- Server-side Retry-After header to damp client retries.

Recommended executive actions:
1) Approve a one-day emergency throughput bump (metered) to buy runway while we finalize the patch.
2) Pre-approve up to 10% credit if we confirm SLA windows were breached during the incident (we'll present final numbers).
3) Authorize priority handling on INF-4321 and an internal postmortem (SEV-incident) with a cross-functional action plan.

Supporting artifacts: logs_20270827.zip, rate_snapshot_08-27.csv, mitigation_playbook.md; INF-4321 JIRA ticket and HubSpot deal HB-2026-987 linked.

If you approve 1 & 2 I will instruct Billing/Revenue Ops to issue the temporary override and coordinate comms.
